q: An office installs 0.5 GPM lavatory faucets, dual-flush 1.1/1.6 GPF toilets, and 1.5 GPM showerheads. Which credit does this support?
options: Energy & Atmosphere: Optimize Energy Performance
Water Efficiency: Indoor Water Use Reduction
Sustainable Sites: Site Water Management
Indoor Environmental Quality: Enhanced Indoor Air Quality
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the WE concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: water efficiency: the reduction and responsible management of potable and process water use; indoor water use reduction: reduction of water used by indoor fixtures, fittings, and appliances; energy performance: the measured or modeled energy use of a building or system; indoor environmental quality: indoor conditions affecting occupant health, comfort, and well-being; indoor air quality: the condition of indoor air with respect to pollutants and ventilation
keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: Water Efficiency: Indoor Water Use Reduction.
logic: Specifying high-efficiency plumbing fixtures (low-flow faucets, dual-flush toilets, low-flow showerheads) is the primary strategy for the Water Efficiency: Indoor Water Use Reduction credit, comparing fixture performance against LEED's calculated baseline.
core_concept: Specifying high-efficiency plumbing fixtures (low-flow faucets, dual-flush toilets, low-flow showerheads) is the primary strategy for the Water Efficiency: Indoor Water Use Reduction credit, comparing fixture performance against LEED's calculated baseline.
evidence_en: Specifying high-efficiency plumbing fixtures (low-flow faucets, dual-flush toilets, low-flow showerheads) is the primary strategy for the Water Efficiency: Indoor Water Use Reduction credit, comparing fixture performance against LEED's calculated baseline.

q: A project team conducts a site survey in pre-design to understand solar access, prevailing winds, and natural drainage. How does this support the integrative process?

It is required to meet local zoning approvals
It informs passive design strategies before major decisions are made
It fulfills site assessment credit requirements only

vocabulary: integrative process: an early collaborative process used to identify system interactions and improve decisions; site assessment: analysis of site conditions used to inform sustainable design decisions; prerequisite: a mandatory requirement that earns no points but is required for certification; credit: an optional LEED requirement that can earn points
keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: It informs passive design strategies before major decisions are made.
logic: Analyzing site conditions early enables the team to develop passive strategies (daylighting, natural ventilation, stormwater management) that reduce reliance on active mechanical systems — the essence of integrative process thinking.
core_concept: Analyzing site conditions early enables the team to develop passive strategies (daylighting, natural ventilation, stormwater management) that reduce reliance on active mechanical systems — the essence of integrative process thinking.
evidence_en: Analyzing site conditions early enables the team to develop passive strategies (daylighting, natural ventilation, stormwater management) that reduce reliance on active mechanical systems — the essence of integrative process thinking.

q: Which is an example of a 'low-impact development' (LID) technique for stormwater management?
options: Increasing slope to direct runoff to storm drains quickly
Bioretention cells (rain gardens) that infiltrate runoff through soil
Covering the entire site with impervious concrete
Installing underground retention tanks that slowly release stormwater to sewers
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the SS concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: sustainable sites: strategies that protect site ecology and manage construction and operational site impacts; site disturbance: physical alteration of soil, vegetation, or existing site conditions
keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: Bioretention cells (rain gardens) that infiltrate runoff through soil.
logic: Bioretention cells collect stormwater runoff and allow it to infiltrate through engineered soil and vegetation, removing pollutants and replenishing groundwater. LID strategies mimic the natural water cycle rather than routing runoff directly to storm drains.
core_concept: Bioretention cells collect stormwater runoff and allow it to infiltrate through engineered soil and vegetation, removing pollutants and replenishing groundwater. LID strategies mimic the natural water cycle rather than routing runoff directly to storm drains.
evidence_en: Bioretention cells collect stormwater runoff and allow it to infiltrate through engineered soil and vegetation, removing pollutants and replenishing groundwater. LID strategies mimic the natural water cycle rather than routing runoff directly to storm drains.

q: Which team composition best exemplifies the integrative process?

MEP engineers meeting separately to coordinate their systems independently
Architect, structural engineer, and contractor meeting only at construction kick-off
Design-build contractor making all decisions independently
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the IP concept and solve this best-fit question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.

keywords: Choose the option that addresses the stated LEED intent most directly, not a secondary benefit; decisive option: Owner, architect, all engineers, and contractor in a pre-design charette.
logic: The integrative process requires early, sustained collaboration across all disciplines, including the owner. A pre-design charette that includes all stakeholders is the hallmark of integrative process implementation.
core_concept: The integrative process requires early, sustained collaboration across all disciplines, including the owner. A pre-design charette that includes all stakeholders is the hallmark of integrative process implementation.
evidence_en: The integrative process requires early, sustained collaboration across all disciplines, including the owner. A pre-design charette that includes all stakeholders is the hallmark of integrative process implementation.

q: A project in a semi-arid climate uses only native plants with no permanent irrigation system. What outdoor water reduction percentage can be claimed?
options: 75% reduction
100% reduction — no irrigation equals 100% reduction from baseline
30% reduction (the LEED minimum)
50% reduction
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the WE concept and solve this threshold question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: baseline: the reference case against which project performance is compared; minimum: the lowest acceptable value or level; water efficiency: reduction and responsible management of indoor, outdoor, and process water use
keywords: Identify the exact minimum, maximum, or numerical threshold requested; decisive value or condition: 100% reduction — no irrigation equals 100% reduction from baseline.
logic: If a project uses no permanent irrigation system (relying only on temporary establishment irrigation or natural rainfall), it claims a 100% reduction from the outdoor water use baseline — the maximum level of outdoor water use reduction available in LEED.
core_concept: If a project uses no permanent irrigation system (relying only on temporary establishment irrigation or natural rainfall), it claims a 100% reduction from the outdoor water use baseline — the maximum level of outdoor water use reduction available in LEED.
evidence_en: If a project uses no permanent irrigation system (relying only on temporary establishment irrigation or natural rainfall), it claims a 100% reduction from the outdoor water use baseline — the maximum level of outdoor water use reduction available in LEED.

logic: The OPR documents what the owner needs the building to achieve — energy use targets, comfort levels, IAQ standards, reliability requirements. The commissioning authority verifies at each project phase that design and construction deliver on these requirements.
core_concept: The OPR documents what the owner needs the building to achieve — energy use targets, comfort levels, IAQ standards, reliability requirements. The commissioning authority verifies at each project phase that design and construction deliver on these requirements.
evidence_en: The OPR documents what the owner needs the building to achieve — energy use targets, comfort levels, IAQ standards, reliability requirements. The commissioning authority verifies at each project phase that design and construction deliver on these requirements.

q: A building's HVAC is found to be cycling excessively during commissioning. What does this indicate and how does commissioning address it?
options: It indicates the building has too many windows
It indicates a design error requiring full equipment replacement
It indicates occupants are using too much energy and need education
It typically signals an oversized system; commissioning adjusts controls
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the EA concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: commissioning: a quality-focused process that verifies systems meet the owner’s project requirements; energy and atmosphere: strategies addressing energy demand, efficiency, refrigerants, and renewable energy; energy efficiency: delivery of the required service with less energy use
keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: It typically signals an oversized system; commissioning adjusts controls.
logic: Excessive cycling often indicates an oversized HVAC system — it reaches setpoint quickly, shuts off, then immediately calls for conditioning again. Commissioning identifies this through performance testing and addresses it by adjusting controls or system configuration to stabilize operation.
core_concept: Excessive cycling often indicates an oversized HVAC system — it reaches setpoint quickly, shuts off, then immediately calls for conditioning again. Commissioning identifies this through performance testing and addresses it by adjusting controls or system configuration to stabilize operation.
evidence_en: Excessive cycling often indicates an oversized HVAC system — it reaches setpoint quickly, shuts off, then immediately calls for conditioning again. q: To maintain LEED Green Associate status, how many continuing education hours are required every two years?

10 hours total, all LEED-specific

q: What is Energy Use Intensity (EUI)?
options: The cost of energy per square foot per year
A normalized measure of annual energy use per floor area (kBtu/sf/yr)
Peak electricity demand of a building in kilowatts
The percentage of a building's energy from renewable sources
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the EA concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: energy and atmosphere: strategies addressing energy demand, efficiency, refrigerants, and renewable energy; energy efficiency: delivery of the required service with less energy use
keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: A normalized measure of annual energy use per floor area (kBtu/sf/yr).
logic: EUI = total annual energy consumed (all fuels) divided by gross floor area. It normalizes energy performance to enable comparison between buildings of different sizes. LEED O+M and ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager use EUI to track and compare building performance.
core_concept: EUI = total annual energy consumed (all fuels) divided by gross floor area. It normalizes energy performance to enable comparison between buildings of different sizes. LEED O+M and ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager use EUI to track and compare building performance.
evidence_en: EUI = total annual energy consumed (all fuels) divided by gross floor area. It normalizes energy performance to enable comparison between buildings of different sizes. LEED O+M and ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager use EUI to track and compare building performance.

q: What is the primary climate benefit of a ground-source heat pump (GSHP) over conventional equipment?
options: GSHPs use no refrigerant
GSHPs can generate electricity as well as provide heating and cooling
GSHPs use stable ground temperatures, reaching higher COP and lower emissions
GSHPs are cheaper to install
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the EA concept and solve this best-fit question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: refrigerant: a working fluid used in cooling and heat-pump systems; energy and atmosphere: strategies addressing energy demand, efficiency, refrigerants, and renewable energy; energy efficiency: delivery of the required service with less energy use
keywords: Choose the option that addresses the stated LEED intent most directly, not a secondary benefit; decisive option: GSHPs use stable ground temperatures, reaching higher COP and lower emissions.
logic: Ground-source heat pumps exchange heat with the stable-temperature ground rather than variable outdoor air, achieving COPs of 3–6 versus 2–4 for air-source equipment. This dramatically reduces energy consumption, peak demand, and GHG emissions across all seasons — especially in extreme weather.
core_concept: Ground-source heat pumps exchange heat with the stable-temperature ground rather than variable outdoor air, achieving COPs of 3–6 versus 2–4 for air-source equipment. This dramatically reduces energy consumption, peak demand, and GHG emissions across all seasons — especially in extreme weather.
evidence_en: Ground-source heat pumps exchange heat with the stable-temperature ground rather than variable outdoor air, achieving COPs of 3–6 versus 2–4 for air-source equipment. This dramatically reduces energy consumption, peak demand, and GHG emissions across all seasons — especially in extreme weather.

q: What is 'variable frequency drive' (VFD) technology and why is it energy-efficient?
options: A variable-rate electricity billing system
A device controlling motor speed by varying frequency — power drops cubically
A type of renewable energy generator
A type of thermostatic control valve
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the EA concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: renewable energy: energy from sources that are naturally replenished; energy and atmosphere: strategies addressing energy demand, efficiency, refrigerants, and renewable energy; energy efficiency: delivery of the required service with less energy use
keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: A device controlling motor speed by varying frequency — power drops cubically.
logic: VFDs allow motors (HVAC fans, pumps) to run at partial speed when full capacity isn't needed. Since power consumption drops with the cube of speed reduction, VFDs can reduce motor energy use by 50–80% compared to constant-speed throttle-controlled motors.
core_concept: VFDs allow motors (HVAC fans, pumps) to run at partial speed when full capacity isn't needed. Since power consumption drops with the cube of speed reduction, VFDs can reduce motor energy use by 50–80% compared to constant-speed throttle-controlled motors.
evidence_en: VFDs allow motors (HVAC fans, pumps) to run at partial speed when full capacity isn't needed. Since power consumption drops with the cube of speed reduction, VFDs can reduce motor energy use by 50–80% compared to constant-speed throttle-controlled motors.

q: A LEED reviewer returns a credit with the ruling 'denied.' What options does the project team have?

Resubmit revised documentation in construction review, or appeal to GBCI
They must request a waiver from USGBC
They must abandon the credit entirely
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the Overview concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.

keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: Resubmit revised documentation in construction review, or appeal to GBCI.
logic: A denied credit can be resubmitted with revised documentation during the construction phase review. If still denied, the team can file a formal GBCI appeal for an independent review at an additional fee.
core_concept: A denied credit can be resubmitted with revised documentation during the construction phase review. If still denied, the team can file a formal GBCI appeal for an independent review at an additional fee.
evidence_en: A denied credit can be resubmitted with revised documentation during the construction phase review. If still denied, the team can file a formal GBCI appeal for an independent review at an additional fee.

q: What is an Environmental Product Declaration (EPD)?

A government certification for low-VOC products

A standardized third-party verified report of a product's lifecycle impacts

keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: A standardized third-party verified report of a product's lifecycle impacts.
logic: An EPD (based on ISO 14025) transparently discloses the lifecycle environmental impacts of a product — global warming potential, ozone depletion, acidification, eutrophication, and more — enabling evidence-based material selection.
core_concept: An EPD (based on ISO 14025) transparently discloses the lifecycle environmental impacts of a product — global warming potential, ozone depletion, acidification, eutrophication, and more — enabling evidence-based material selection.
evidence_en: An EPD (based on ISO 14025) transparently discloses the lifecycle environmental impacts of a product — global warming potential, ozone depletion, acidification, eutrophication, and more — enabling evidence-based material selection.

core_concept: LEED BD+C certifies design and construction intent. Actual ongoing performance depends on operations, maintenance, and occupant behavior. LEED O+M with the Arc platform provides a pathway to verify and communicate continued sustainability performance over time.

A program certifying entire city blocks at once
A streamlined program for portfolio owners certifying many similar buildings
A program for very large single buildings over 1 million square feet

keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: A streamlined program for portfolio owners certifying many similar buildings.
logic: LEED Volume Certification allows organizations with many similar buildings (retailers, school districts, hotel chains) to review one prototype design, then apply standardized documentation to subsequent buildings, dramatically reducing certification cost and effort across the portfolio.

q: A project is located outside the United States and the referenced ASHRAE 90.1 standard does not apply locally. What is the correct approach?
options: The team skips all Energy & Atmosphere credits
Use an equivalent local energy standard, or submit a CIR for an alternative path
The team applies U.S. standards regardless of local context
The project cannot pursue LEED certification
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the Overview concept and solve this exception question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: credit: an optional LEED requirement that can earn points; certification: third-party confirmation that a project satisfies applicable LEED requirements; LEED: a third-party green building rating and certification system
keywords: Identify the exception or the option that does not satisfy the common LEED condition; decisive option: Use an equivalent local energy standard, or submit a CIR for an alternative path.
logic: LEED is designed for global use. When a referenced U.S. standard doesn't apply internationally, teams may use equivalent local standards. If equivalency is not clearly established, a CIR provides GBCI's project-specific ruling on the alternative compliance path.
core_concept: LEED is designed for global use. When a referenced U.S. standard doesn't apply internationally, teams may use equivalent local standards. If equivalency is not clearly established, a CIR provides GBCI's project-specific ruling on the alternative compliance path.
evidence_en: LEED is designed for global use. When a referenced U.S. standard doesn't apply internationally, teams may use equivalent local standards. If equivalency is not clearly established, a CIR provides GBCI's project-specific ruling on the alternative compliance path.

q: Which of the following best describes the 'triple bottom line' in the context of LEED and green building?
options: A method scoring buildings equally on energy, water, and waste
A framework evaluating environmental, social, and economic dimensions together
A financial accounting method requiring three separate audits
A LEED requirement to submit three separate review applications

keywords: Choose the option that addresses the stated LEED intent most directly, not a secondary benefit; decisive option: A framework evaluating environmental, social, and economic dimensions together.
logic: The triple bottom line (TBL) measures sustainability across three dimensions: environmental impact, social equity, and economic viability. LEED credits broadly align with TBL by addressing environmental performance, occupant health (social), and reduced operating costs (economic).
core_concept: The triple bottom line (TBL) measures sustainability across three dimensions: environmental impact, social equity, and economic viability. LEED credits broadly align with TBL by addressing environmental performance, occupant health (social), and reduced operating costs (economic).
evidence_en: The triple bottom line (TBL) measures sustainability across three dimensions: environmental impact, social equity, and economic viability. LEED credits broadly align with TBL by addressing environmental performance, occupant health (social), and reduced operating costs (economic).

q: What distinguishes a LEED 'credit' from a LEED 'prerequisite' in terms of project strategy?

logic: The fundamental LEED structure: prerequisites set a non-negotiable floor of sustainability performance (mandatory, no points). Credits allow teams to strategically pursue additional sustainability improvements based on project circumstances, with points awarded for each credit achieved.

q: A LEED project team submits for design review and gets back a 'pending' status for one credit. What does 'pending' mean?

The credit has been denied and must be appealed
It cannot be reviewed yet — it requires construction-phase documentation
The reviewer is waiting for the team to pay additional fees
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the Overview concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.

keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: It cannot be reviewed yet — it requires construction-phase documentation.

core_concept: 'Pending' means the credit is construction-phase dependent and cannot be evaluated based on design documents alone. The team must provide construction-phase documentation (e.g., actual waste diversion receipts, IAQ test results) before a final ruling can be given.

q: What is the role of the 'LEED Coordinator' on a project team?

The LEED Coordinator approves all contractor submittals
A team member coordinating documentation, credit tracking, and GBCI communication
The LEED Coordinator is a mandatory GBCI employee assigned to each project
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the Overview concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: energy model: a simulation used to estimate and compare building energy performance; credit: an optional LEED requirement that can earn points; documentation: records used to demonstrate compliance with a LEED requirement
keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: A team member coordinating documentation, credit tracking, and GBCI communication.

q: In LEED V5, what does the concept of 'performance verification' add beyond traditional LEED design-intent documentation?
options: It requires buildings to hire a third-party energy auditor each year
It replaces energy modeling with utility bill analysis only
It is only applicable to LEED O+M projects
It requires measuring and verifying actual post-occupancy performance
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the Overview concept and solve this documentation question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: energy model: a simulation used to estimate and compare building energy performance; documentation: records used to demonstrate compliance with a LEED requirement; LEED: a third-party green building rating and certification system
keywords: Distinguish the technical requirement from the document or evidence that verifies it; decisive evidence: It requires measuring and verifying actual post-occupancy performance.
logic: LEED V5 closes the loop between design intent and real-world results. Performance verification through metered data, occupant surveys, and post-occupancy assessments ensures buildings actually deliver on sustainability promises — addressing the gap between modeled and actual performance.
